title: Scaffolding & Import Boundaries
subject: main
summary: This architecture tries to achieve: consistency and decoupability.

axioms.text: Apps mount, wire, and inject. Product logic lives in [[slice|slices]], never in the app shell. [[slice|Slices]] are **[[seed slice|seed slices]]** `apps/main/slices/seed/<m>/`,  or **[[product slice|product slices]]** `apps/main/slices/product/<f>/`
Every [[slice]] is built the same way.
sub: **Structure:** [[seed slice|seed slices]] and [[product slice|product slices]] are built identically: same API, web and mobile layers and patterns.

axioms.text: Every [[slice]] relates to the app the same way.
sub: **Imports:** a slice imports only libs and packages. Configs, slice infra (db), [[leaf adapter|leaf adapters]] (toast, i18n) and other assets are [[injection|injected]] by the app, only at the [[mount]] point.
**Exports:** the app imports only what a slice exposes through its [[public surface]].

**Orchestration:** the app mounts slices and owns all wiring between them. Slices emit [[lifecycle hook|lifecycle hooks]] with facts and intentions; the app decides what to do with them, potentially calling another slice's [[public surface]].

axioms.text: Slices differ in one thing only: whether they may reach each other.
sub: A **[[seed slice]]** never reaches another seed slice — no deep imports, and no service calling another seed slice's service, not even through its [[public surface]]. Only the app may call a seed slice's public surface. A seed slice carries no knowledge of its neighbours, which is what lets a different project take it.
**[[product slice|Product slices]]** may reach each other directly. A product slice exists only for this product, so it is a code-organization convention, not an import boundary.

purpose.intro: This architecture tries to achieve: consistency and decoupability.
points: **Consistency:** a developer working in any [[slice]] reads the same structure and the same patterns, no per-slice dialects, no relearning.
**Decoupability:** removing a seed slice should be simple: remove the seed slice, its [[mount]] and its wiring, and anything that still breaks is a declared need, breaking where it was declared.
purpose.note: Both properties come from the same boundaries: self-contained seed slices, injected dependencies, app-owned orchestration.

claims.text: The app reaches a [[slice]] only through its barrels: `api/index.ts` · `web/index.ts` · `shared/index.ts` (the wire contract) · `api/models/index.ts` (db-client aggregation only). Everything behind a barrel is internal — a deep import is a violation.
At [[mount]], the app [[injection|injects]] what the slice declared it needs: configs, db, adapters, other slices' capabilities.
The mount returns the slice's capabilities — services, hooks, components, routes. Only the app holds them; another slice can declare a need, and the app decides whether to inject.

Wiring and plumbing live in the app: a slice emits [[lifecycle hook|lifecycle hooks]], the app listens and decides, potentially calling another slice's capability. A slice never listens to another slice directly.
Env vars drive what mounts: which slices mount and which configs inject come from env vars, never hardcode. The pointer to which config is consumed lives outside the config object.
A [[library]] never imports another library — libraries import node modules only.

claims.text: Imports are scoped by [[tier]]: `@configs/…` · `@libs/…` · `@modules/…` ([[seed slice|seed slices]]) · `@product/…` ([[product slice|product slices]]) · `@apps/…`.
Platform belongs in the [[package]] name, never in the scope: `@libs/web-components`, `@libs/mobile-components`.

Every level has a `shared/` folder holding what its children consume: repo `shared/` ([[library|libs]] + [[seed slice|seed slices]], consumed by all apps) · `apps/main/slices/product/shared/` (shared by all product slices) · `<seed slice>/shared/` and `<product slice>/shared/` (across that [[slice]]'s [[slice app|slice apps]]). Shared code sits at the nearest level above all its consumers — never in `lib` folders. Placement ladder (first fit wins): pure data → `configs/` · generic engine → `shared/libs/` · reusable [[slice]] slice → `apps/main/slices/seed/` · this-product [[slice]] slice → `apps/main/slices/product/` · wiring → app shell.

examples.title: A UI capability — the member picker
examples.text: Type-ahead over the users the current user may share with, resolving to a user id, or to an email address when that person has no account yet. It lives in `user-organization-mgmt` because UOM is the only slice that knows users, memberships and org visibility — one declarer, and no product slice reimplements it. It reaches other slices by export: UOM puts it on its web [[public surface]], and the app [[injection|injects]] it into the product slice that declared the need.

├── components/members/MemberPicker.tsx    the capability
└── index.ts                               the public surface

snippets.caption: How UOM exports it — the barrel is the whole surface; nothing else is reachable
How the app injects it — the app names UOM, the product slice never does

examples.title: A service capability — resolving user ids
examples.text: Slices store user ids, not users: a song row carries an owner id, an audit row an actor id. To render who did something, the caller hands the ids to UOM and gets back name and image. UOM stays the only reader of its own tables — the caller never sees the repository and never learns where the data sits. The seam exists in the repo already, but is seed slice-internal: making it consumable by another slice means putting it on the mount result, which is the whole act of exporting a capability.

snippets.caption: The seam, as written today
What the app can hand out — the service handles on UOM's mount result
What song declares it needs — its own words, no UOM types
How the app injects it — it satisfies song's declaration with UOM

reference.topic: API: every slice has the same folders

claims.text: API folders are the same in every slice: `middlewares/ routes/ services/ repositories/ models/` — identical at every level (seed slice, product slice, app). Always folders, even for one file; scaffolding never changes shape. What lives inside each folder is [[backend-composition|Backend Composition]]'s subject.

reference.topic: Web: who owns the router, the shell and the page

claims.text: Web folders are the same in every slice: `routes/ pages/ components/ hooks/ providers/`. What lives inside each folder is [[frontend-composition|Frontend Composition]]'s subject.

A [[slice]] proposes routes as pure data, page inside — access intent, title, icon; never a [[shell]] decision. A slice never exports a page by name. The app owns all routing and mounts every route it accepts.
The app decides per route which [[shell]] applies. A [[page]] belongs to the [[slice]] that contributed it, or to the app.

Navigation follows the shared rule: it is owned at the most specific level that covers all its targets. A menu over pages of one [[slice]] belongs to that slice. A menu whose targets span slices belongs to the app — the slices contribute their pages and nav entries, the app assembles and mounts.

examples.title: /my/settings/security, end to end
examples.text: UOM contributes the route as data — page, access intent, title and icon inside. The app mounts it under the shell it chose for that route and assembles its nav from the contributed data, in whatever order and shape it wants. Today the app instead hardcodes every nav entry in its own config — a violation, logged in decisions.
